sentences.text: The present petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioner seeking quashment of Crime No.383/2019 registered at Police Station Ambah, District Morena for offence punishable under Sections 420, 272, 273, 120-B of IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of Food Safety Act and all consequential proceedings.

2. The prosecution case, in short is that , as per the prosecution story on 01.08.2019 food safety officer Rekha Soni submitted one written letter for registration of FIR alleging that on 30.07.2019,
one go-down of co-accused Sunil Agarwal behind the Jai Ambe Garden was sealed by her.

Thereafter, on 31.07.2019 Rekha Soni/food safety officer and other food safety officer-Anil Pratap Singh Parishar and Tehsildar Ramnivas Sharma & Ors unlocked the said go-down of co-accused Sunil Agarwal and during inspection 1153 bags of Dexotrin powder and six iron drums which were filled with RM Chemical NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 2 MCRC-15529-2023 were kept in the go-down.
Thereafter, the inspecting authorities had drawn the sample and of Dexotrin powder and RM chemical in absence of co- accused Sunil Agarwal.

The aforesaid samples had been sent to the food laboratory Bhopal for testing so, it was alleged that co-accused Sunil Agarwal had stored the Malto Dexotin powder and RM chemical for promoting the food adulteration business and further alleged that the co- accused is gaining illegal advantage and such business which is harmful for the health of general public.

During investigation of the case one written letter has been submitted to police authority by food safety officer Rekha Soni on 14-10-2019, in which it has been alleged that on 27-9-2019 Mittal laboratory and chemical supplier has been inspected by food and administrative department at the time of checking, petitioner was present who stated that he sells machinery equipment and chemicals and same was stored Sachin Mittal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47124589/

sentences.text:
1 thereafter, inspecting team perused the document which were available at petitioner's premises and authority had got the knowledge that proprietor of said firm sold the Malto dexotin powder,
skimmed milk powder and RM chemical, hydrogen peroxide, reji, refined palm oil and other substance which were used for adulterant milk thus, however, no such article which mention hereinabove have been found in petitioner premises, only bills of the applicant's firm were seized therefore, the applicant has been arrayed as an accused in the offence by alleging that the applicant helped to the co-accused in his business of chemical for promoting the adulterated milk and except such things there was no iota of evidence available with the inspecting authority by which in any manner the applicant could be dragged NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 3 MCRC-15529-2023 in the offence.

The investigation against the present applicant was pending,
therefore, charge sheet has been filed only against the co-accused.

3 . From perusal of the GST registration as well as shop act license of the applicant and name of the applicant firm itself reflect that the applicant is running the business as chemical supplier and under any law no restriction has been imposed by legislature to sell the chemical and dexotrin powder and since beginning authority was very well aware that applicant is selling the chemical and other food products.

In the entire FIR, no consumer has made any complaint that the applicant is selling the said product for adulterating the food articles, even no food articles were found from the applicants premises but in spite of this the shameful action has been taken by the officer just under the pressure of police whereas, they were not having any iota of evidence which restricted to the applicant for selling the chemicals and dexotrin powder to the shopkeepers and consumers.
4 .

There is no allegation leveled against the present applicant in the entire FIR, nor the name of applicant has been reflected but during investigation on seizing the bill of applicant's firm, he has been arrayed as an accused whereas main allegation for storage of chemicals is against co- accused Sunil Agarwal that being so, in view of the above reasons applicant deserves to be exonerated from the allegation leveled against him.
5 . It has been alleged against the applicant that he sells the chemical and other substance in the market and which is offence u/s 272,273 and 420 of IPC.

Approach of the inspecting authority is highly misconceived and shameful because once the applicant has obtained his registration under the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 4 MCRC-15529-2023 GST for selling chemical and other substance and not only he is authorized to sell the chemical but also his firm has been registered in the name of Mittal Laboratory and Chemical Supplier then in such circumstances if any restriction was made by the Legislature, then definitely registration of the applicant firm would not have been made by the GST Department in their records.

Even otherwise, the applicant is having a shop act registration which issued by the concerning department in the name of Mittal Laboratory and chemical Supplier thus, applicant can trade the business of those substances which are added in the food.
In spite of this why the applicant has been prosecuted, is not understandable.

The action taken by the inspecting authority as well as the police seems to be prima facie illegal,
arbitrary and violation of article 14 and 19 (1) G of the Constitution of India.
In such circumstances strict direction is required to be issued against the respondent department and against the police authority.

The same matter has been considered by this court in the case of Balmukund Gard Vs.
State of M.P. vide order dated 23.11.2019 passed in M.Cr.C. No.39005/2019.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the petitioner has approached this Court invoking its inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C., contending that the FIR and consequent proceedings are NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 5 MCRC-15529-2023 malicious, frivolous and an abuse of process of law.
It is submitted that the alleged offences under the Food Safety and Standards Act are compoundable and triable by a designated authority and the invocation of IPC provisions is unwarranted.

It is further submitted that that no direct evidence connects the petitioner with adulteration or misbranding and continuation of proceedings would cause irreparable harm to his reputation and business.

Hence, he prays that petition be allowed and the FIR registered at Crime No.383/2019 at Police Station Ambah, District Morena for offence punishable under Sections 420, 272, 273, 120-B of IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of Food Safety Act and all consequential proceedings be quashed regarding the present petitioner.

8. Learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, opposed the petition by submitting that the allegations reveal a systematic and deliberate act of preparing and selling adulterated spurious milk,
which is dangerous to public health.

It is further submitted that the acts of deception and misrepresentation fall squarely under Section 420 IPC and the presence of conspiracy and adulteration attracts the provisions of Sections 272, 273, and 120-B IPC, in addition to the statutory offences under the Food Safety and Standards Act.
Hence, the proceedings cannot be quashed at the threshold.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
10.
In the case in hand, it is undisputed that the present applicant is involved in sale of the aforesaid chemical substances.
The criminal proceedings were initially initiated against the co-accused Sunil Agrawal.
But, to establish the chain and to find the apex perpetrator, the present NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 6 MCRC-15529-2023 petitioner was intercepted.
During the course of the Investigation, the petitioner approached this Court and the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 18.04.2023, granted interim stay to the present petitioner.
11. Due to the aforesaid interim stay, the charge sheet was filed in respect of co-accused only but the investigation in respect of present petitioner was kept pending.
Therefore, it is clear that the investigation in respect of the present petitioner has not completed.

12. It is also worth mentioning that the petitioner was possessing license to operate the alleged establishment/shop but, the petitioner has failed to produce any authorization or license to sell such chemicals, inappropriate usages of which can cause damage to public health.

sentences.text: It is also evident from record that there was a huge quantity of supply of such chemicals by the present petitioner to the co-accused and that too was in regular span.
Such huge quantity of regular supply in a village calls the attention of this Court that the fact cannot be denied that prima facie case is made out.
14. Since, the petitioner had obtained the interim stay from this Court, therefore, the investigation has not been carried out in respect of present petitioner, nor charge-sheet has been filed.

Therefore,
petition appears to be premature.

15. The power of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is of a very wide amplitude, but it is to be exercised sparingly, with caution and only to prevent abuse of the process of law or to secure the ends of justice.

16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 7 MCRC-15529-2023 [(1992) Supp (1) SCC 335] has categorically laid down the parameters under which the High Court may exercise its inherent powers to quash criminal proceedings.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court held that such power should be invoked only where the allegations do not disclose any cognizable offence, are absurd or inherently improbable, or where proceedings are manifestly attended with malafide intention.

1 7 . In the present case, the material collected during investigation, including the chemical analysis report, prima facie indicates that the food items were adulterated and unsafe for human consumption.
The seizure, laboratory report and the chain of distribution established during investigation connect the petitioner with the alleged offence.
Therefore, the allegations, if taken at face value, clearly disclose the commission of cognizable offences under the said Acts.
18. Applying the above principles to the present case, this Court finds that the ingredients of cheating, adulteration and criminal conspiracy are prima facie made out against the petitioner.
The acts alleged, if proved, amount to offences punishable under both the IPC and the Food Safety and Standards Act.
The question as to whether both sets of provisions can simultaneously operate is a mixed question of law and fact, which can only be adjudicated upon during trial and not at the stage of quashing.

19. Considering the gravity of allegations, public health implications and prima facie material on record, this Court finds no ground to invoke inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of the proceedings in the present case.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 8 MCRC-15529-2023 20.
Accordingly, the petition being premature is hereby dismissed.
21. A copy of this order be sent of SHO Police Station Ambah District Morena for information and necessary action.
